vasant-shinde-archaeologist.name: Vasant Shinde
vasant-shinde-archaeologist.summary: Indian archaeologist who excavated Rakhigarhi from 2011 to 2016 and led a 2019 genetic study of a Harappan skeleton, though he later publicly endorsed the rival Out of India theory.

mehrgarh.name: Mehrgarh
mehrgarh.summary: Neolithic archaeological site on the Kacchi Plain of Balochistan, Pakistan, discovered in 1974, with a farming settlement dated to around 7000 BCE.

kacchi-plain.name: Kacchi Plain
kacchi-plain.summary: Low-lying plain in Balochistan, Pakistan, also called Kach Gandava, home to the early Neolithic site of Mehrgarh.

zebu.name: Zebu
zebu.summary: A humped subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia, well adapted to heat and raised throughout the tropics as draught, dairy and beef animals.

balochistan.name: Balochistan
balochistan.summary: A historical, arid region of desert and mountains split among Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan, populated mainly by ethnic Baloch and strategically important for its coastline and mineral wealth.

bhimbetka-rock-shelters.name: Bhimbetka rock shelters
bhimbetka-rock-shelters.summary: An archaeological site in central India with over 750 rock shelters, some inhabited more than 100,000 years ago, showing the earliest traces of human life in India.

raisen-district.name: Raisen district
raisen-district.summary: A district of Madhya Pradesh, India, whose Sanchi Town hosts the Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

deccan-plateau.name: Deccan Plateau
deccan-plateau.summary: A large plateau covering much of southern India, bounded by the Eastern and Western Ghats, formed partly from ancient lava flows and crossed by major rivers such as the Godavari and Krishna.

v-s-wakankar.name: V. S. Wakankar
v-s-wakankar.summary: An Indian archaeologist (1919–1988) who discovered the Bhimbetka rock caves in 1957, later named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

burzahom-archaeological-site.name: Burzahom
burzahom-archaeological-site.summary: An archaeological site in Kashmir, India, with cultural layers from 3000 to 1000 BCE showing a shift from underground Neolithic dwellings to mudbrick structures.

kot-diji.name: Kot Diji
kot-diji.summary: Ancient Indus Valley Civilisation site on the Indus River opposite Mohenjo-daro, occupied from about 3300 BCE, with a citadel built about 12 metres above the surrounding area.

mohenjo-daro.name: Mohenjo-daro
mohenjo-daro.summary: One of the largest cities of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation, built around 2500 BCE and home to at least 40,000 people before being abandoned by about 1700 BCE.

bolan-pass.name: Bolan Pass
bolan-pass.summary: A natural mountain gateway through Balochistan, Pakistan, long used by traders, invaders and nomadic tribes as a route into South Asia.

soanian.name: Soanian
soanian.summary: A prehistoric stone-tool culture of the Siwalik Hills region across modern India, Nepal and Pakistan, named after Pakistan's Soan Valley.

sivalik-hills.name: Sivalik Hills
sivalik-hills.summary: A mountain range of the outer Himalayas, also called the Churia Hills, known for numerous fossils and home to the Soanian Middle Paleolithic culture.

girnar.name: Girnar
girnar.summary: An ancient hill near Junagadh, Gujarat, sacred to Jains as the place where the 22nd Tirthankar attained enlightenment and nirvana.

bhirrana.name: Bhirrana
bhirrana.summary: An archaeological site in Haryana, India, whose earliest layers have been dated to the 8th to 7th millennium BCE, predating the Indus Valley civilisation.

ghaggar-hakra-river.name: Ghaggar-Hakra River
ghaggar-hakra-river.summary: Seasonal river in India and Pakistan whose middle course, once fed by stronger monsoons, was home to many sites of the Mature Indus Valley Civilisation around 2600–1900 BCE.

kupgal-petroglyphs.name: Kupgal petroglyphs
kupgal-petroglyphs.summary: Rock art site in Karnataka, India, with thousands of Neolithic or Stone Age petroglyphs, including unusual rock formations that make musical sounds when struck.
